I am 69 and my household is small, so I will keep things steady and practical instead of trying anything risky. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on stable water at the key stages and use improved seed so I can get dependable stands and yield. For wheat, I will keep fertilizer moderate and balanced, with more attention to nitrogen because that drives growth, but I will still add phosphorus and some potassium to keep the crop steady. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage on a small farm and fits my usual rotation. I will spray only as much as I think I need to keep weeds, insects, and disease from getting ahead of me. After wheat harvest, I will plant maize on the same land, again using improved seed, somewhat higher nitrogen than wheat, and fewer irrigations because the summer season usually gives me more moisture, though I still have the well if the rain is not enough. I will keep the plan simple, labor-saving, and reliable because that is what I would trust on my own farm this year.
